<a id="acquisition-checklist-source-acquisition-and-observation-reliability"></a>

# Acquisition checklist: source acquisition and observation reliability

**Purpose**: Review completeness, clarity and consistency of source acquisition requirements before acceptance of the functional specification.

**Created**: 2026-09-15

**Feature**: [Source acquisition specification](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the official `speckit-checklist` skill from the approved source acquisition scope.

**Review ownership**: This requirements-quality review artifact is reviewer-owned. An item must only be marked `[x]` when the reviewer considers the criterion satisfied.

**Marker meaning**: `[x]` means requirement quality has been reviewed and found satisfactory; it does not mean implementation is complete.

<a id="requirement-completeness"></a>

## Requirement completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are the supported sources, retention of CSV acquisition, five exclusions and boundaries excluding unrelated competitions explicit? [Completeness, Specification §FR-001–FR-003]
- [ ] CHK002 Is coverage of every phase of the three professional championships explicitly distinguished from observed V1 behavior and samples of future availability? [Completeness, Specification §FR-002, §Evidence and decision traceability]
- [ ] CHK003 Are source preparation/launch independent of mapping, pre-mapping acquisition limited to pool/pack discovery without calendar/result staging, collection screens free of classification readiness/mapping shortcuts, and simultaneous seasons, initial reconstruction before closure and terminal typed closure distinguished? [Completeness, FR-007, FR-046–FR-049, FR-055]
- [ ] CHK004 Are pack classification, full individual overrides, active seasons/divisions and catalog-based discovery specified without manual exclusions or public-visibility gating? [Completeness, FR-008–FR-010]
- [ ] CHK005 Does the observation handoff define context, times, native references, values, scope, completeness and reasons without choosing a transport or storage design? [Completeness, Specification §FR-021–FR-023]

<a id="requirement-clarity"></a>

## Requirement clarity

- [ ] CHK006 Is a usable catalog distinguished from a successful HTTP response, an error page, a partial read and a genuinely empty catalog? [Clarity, Specification §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK007 Is immediately stopping collection from a source after confirmed catalog absence distinguished from continuing to use valid same-season references during discovery failure and from F02 visibility? [Clarity, Specification §FR-005–FR-006, §FR-019]
- [ ] CHK008 Is reuse of the latest known references limited to earlier successful discovery in the same season and current eligibility, ending on confirmed absence, without invented references or fallback to old configuration? [Clarity, Specification §FR-006, §FR-031, §FR-034]
- [ ] CHK009 Are globally invalid calendars, isolated match anomalies, invalid secondary fields and normally missing or future-slot information distinguished? [Clarity, Specification §FR-011–FR-016]
- [ ] CHK010 Are contradictory observations from the same source distinguished from identical repetitions, code reuse across seasons and provider priorities? [Clarity, Specification §FR-013, §A09]
- [ ] CHK011 Are cadence windows, unknown kickoff, corrected kickoff, overruns and scheduled deadlines specified without falsely promising publication freshness? [Clarity, Specification §FR-030–FR-031, §FR-035]

<a id="requirement-consistency"></a>

## Requirement consistency

- [ ] CHK012 Are independence between calendars, standings and providers and preservation of previous state compatible with usable partial inputs and the prohibition on absence-based withdrawals after incomplete processing? [Consistency, Specification §FR-012, §FR-017–FR-020]
- [ ] CHK013 Are single qualified current emptiness, false empty, incomplete integration and protected closed-season history distinguished without a confirmation counter? [Consistency, FR-019–FR-020, A13]
- [ ] CHK014 Are acquisition success, integration failure and claims that application data has been updated consistently separated? [Consistency, Specification §FR-022, §FR-039, §FR-043]
- [ ] CHK015 Are reliable cycle-start settings and division or classification changes at the next cycle distinct from permitted reference reuse and retained published classification, without collection resuming after a refused restoration? [Consistency, Specification §FR-006, §FR-008, §FR-033–FR-034, §A06]
- [ ] CHK016 Are family-only relaunch, absence of duplicate executions and absence of implicit unpausing consistent across competition, club and geocoding commands? [Consistency, Specification §FR-028, §FR-032–FR-036]

<a id="scenario-and-recovery-coverage"></a>

## Scenario and recovery coverage

- [ ] CHK017 Are a failed club page and successful but empty or ambiguous geocoding distinguished from technical failure, with explicit retry consequences? [Coverage, Specification §FR-024–FR-029, §A19–A22]
- [ ] CHK018 Does geocoding follow the effective F02 locality after corrections and restrictions, and does manual relaunch include unchanged unresolved addresses while excluding unnecessary recalculation of valid results? [Coverage, Specification §FR-026–FR-028, §A20–A21 ; F02 §A36–A38]
- [ ] CHK019 Is the first failed competition cycle enough to open a grouped incident, with no failure counter and positive recovery evidence? [Coverage, FR-041–FR-044, A29–A30]
- [ ] CHK020 Are the immediate structural-anomaly incident threshold, the first-failed-competition-cycle trigger and the 24-hour threshold distinct and consistent with normal source cadence? [Coverage, Specification §FR-040–FR-042]
- [ ] CHK021 Is actual recovery defined by usable evidence from the affected scope, excluding pause, season closure and unrelated success? [Coverage, Specification §FR-043, §A30]
- [ ] CHK022 Are incident persistence, notifications limited to opening and recovery, and grouped reports of new items or classification needs specified without imposing a new incident platform? [Coverage, Specification §FR-044–FR-045]
- [ ] CHK023 Is initial reconstruction restricted to prepared seasons before closure, retaining classification/coverage/permission/context checks and archive-gap reporting, without global pauses or post-closure recollection? [Coverage, FR-020, FR-046–FR-049, FR-055; A34–A36]

<a id="acceptance-criteria-quality"></a>

## Acceptance criteria quality

- [ ] CHK024 Is each functional requirement covered by concrete scenarios, including cycle counting, local match contradictions, partial outcomes and actual recovery? [Traceability, Specification §Inventory coverage, §A08–A09, §A29–A30]
- [ ] CHK025 Are success criteria measurable as user or operator outcomes with explicit provider, configuration and cadence assumptions? [Measurability, Specification §SC-001–SC-008, §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK026 Are primary, exception, refusal, empty or partial data, and recovery scenarios represented without claiming that V2 acceptance tests have already run? [Coverage, Specification §User scenarios and validation, §Edge cases]

<a id="dependencies-privacy-and-scope"></a>

## Dependencies, privacy and scope

- [ ] CHK027 Are permissions explicit and distinct from live-link moderator authority, while their assignment remains in F12? [Completeness, Specification §FR-038, §Cross-feature dependencies]
- [ ] CHK028 Are useful observations and diagnostic metadata distinguished from raw archives and personal data prohibited in diagnostics, with retention assigned to F11/F13? [Consistency, Specification §FR-021–FR-023, §FR-025]
- [ ] CHK029 Does every unresolved cross-domain decision have an identified owner and a defined F01 input or constraint rather than being left to the implementer? [Dependencies, Specification §Cross-feature dependencies]
- [ ] CHK030 Are source-review limits, explicit V2 changes, shared-model considerations, Figma follow-ups and the complete-corpus gate stated without imposing a technical architecture? [Scope, Specification §Assumptions, §Evidence and decision traceability, §Cross-feature dependencies]

## Notes

- This checklist reviews writing, not correct software operation. All newly generated markers are deliberately unchecked.
- Add reviewer findings beside the affected items and link the relevant requirement or scenario.
- `speckit-implement` uses checklist state as a gate and must not change the markers.
- [requirements.md](requirements.md) follows the separate built-in lifecycle maintained by Specify and Clarify.
